label: cor:ftc_eval
title: Evaluation of integrals via antiderivatives
statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $\texttt{uIcc}\; a\; b = [\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and let $F$ be an antiderivative of $f$ on $\mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$ (i.e.\ $\texttt{IsAntiderivativeOn}\; F\; f\; (\min(a,b))\; (\max(a,b))$) that is continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$. Then
    \[
      \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a).
    \]
proof: By Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_is_antiderivative}, the function $G(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$ is an antiderivative of $f$ on $\mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:antiderivatives_diff_constant}, $F - G$ is constant on $\mathrm{Icc}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$, so $F(b) - G(b) = F(a) - G(a)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_func_at_base}, $G(a) = 0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:constant_diff_rearrangement}, $G(b) = F(b) - F(a)$, and since $G(b) = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx$, the result follows.
